notes: From the homeowner's top-down plan (annotated: the wing's top edge is 6', not 10') + site photos. House along the top with the brick chimney projecting into the chimney bay; the wing's inner edge is the brick house wall with the chimney's angled faces (two 10'5" diagonals, ~2' deep at the middle) — framed here as a straight wall, so the diagonal rim cuts are not counted. Left end open (rail). Bays left to right: wing 6' x 30' (wall 30' back), middle bay 9' wide with its wall 10' back, chimney bay 10'6" wide with the chimney face 6'6" back, right bay with the wall 10'6" back. Right bay set to 11'6" so the bays sum to the plan's 37' overall: the plan's 26'6" for the porch cover cannot also be true — if the deck right of the chimney really is 26'6", the deck is 52' wide and this takeoff is ~40% short. FIELD MEASURE FIRST. Plan says 8' high at the left, 6' at the right: frame at 8', posts cut to grade. Plan says joists AND boards run perpendicular to the house, which cannot both be true — GSX frame kept (joists perpendicular, boards parallel); flipping to perpendicular boards is a rerun. Existing deck (all of it) is demo'd: stained wood, black aluminum balusters with a flat drink-rail cap, 6x6 posts. Existing translucent-panel cover on 6x6 posts stands on the deck by the door: take down and reset on the new frame (RFI, not priced). Existing straight 4' stair down along the house siding to a concrete pad — put on the right end (end:right) next to the house, one rail; confirm which end.

site.notes: Pikes Peak Regional Building Dept: 30 psf snow, 30" frost, Vult 115 mph east of the foothills — confirm the lot is not in the 130-150 mph special wind region.
